research.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Causal XAI for Suspicious Activity Detection in Smart Surveillance Systems
research.summary: A research-oriented framework that improves the transparency, reliability, and trustworthiness of suspicious activity detection in surveillance video. Conventional deep learning surveillance systems classify suspicious activity accurately but operate as black boxes, offering little insight into why a clip was flagged. This project integrates Explainable AI (XAI) and Causal AI with a deep learning detection model to address that gap.
research.approach: A custom dataset was built by extracting and manually selecting frames representing suspicious activities (fighting, robbery, stealing, explosion, shooting) alongside normal activity. A ResNet50-based CNN learns visual features and classifies the activity. XAI techniques highlight which visual regions and features drove the prediction, while causal analysis investigates the underlying cause-and-effect factors behind the detected activity — combining predictive modeling, visual explanation, and causal reasoning for more trustworthy interpretations.
research.context: Final-year BCT research, alongside applied engineering work in agentic systems and RAG (Sykra Research).
